title: Trait matching affects the probability of nectar robbing in plant–pollinator networks
decision_basis: Primary paper directly models visitor-flower trait mismatch / barrier against legitimate-versus-robbery route; eligible structurally but already contributes to the primary standardized network and must not be counted as an additional independent supporting program.
notes: Keep outside supporting-program independence count; preserve as network overlap.

title: Long corolla flowers in Tropical Andes favour nectar robbing by the Black Metaltail hummingbird: A study using citizen science and field observations
decision_basis: Primary research measures corolla length independently and classifies hummingbird foraging events as legitimate or nectar robbing; quantitative association is reported.
notes: Eligibility frozen before formal direction coding.

title: When Bigger Is not Better: Corolla Length Increases Nectar Robbing in Aloe secundiflora Engl. (Asphodelaceae)
decision_basis: Primary research measures corolla tube length and models flower-level nectar-robbery probability; route-resolved robbery outcome and quantitative predictor test are present.
notes: Eligibility frozen before formal direction coding.

title: Pollinators and nectar robbers cause directional selection for large spur circle in Impatiens oxyanthera (Balsaminaceae)
decision_basis: Primary study measures floral geometry and models nectar-robber visit frequency as a mediator/outcome of floral traits; quantitative geometry-to-robbing path is directly estimated.
notes: Eligibility frozen before formal direction coding.

title: Corolla stickiness prevents nectar robbing in Erica
decision_basis: Robbery experiment contrasts floral stickiness/adhesive strength. Corolla length and shape are analysed as correlates of stickiness, not as the focal independent predictor of the robbery outcome under the frozen access-geometry contract.
notes: Retain as mechanistic context, not formal direct geometry program.

title: Morphological specialisation for primary nectar robbing in a pollen specialist mining bee (Hymenoptera, Andrenidae)
decision_basis: Study measures specialised bee proboscis morphology and describes approximately 90 robbery visits, but does not provide the required quantitative comparison/model of an access variable against robbery route probability/frequency across independent units.
notes: Morphological adaptation evidence is contextual, not a codable geometry-to-robbery directional test.

title: Biting the hand that feeds you: wedge-billed hummingbird is a nectar robber of a sicklebill-adapted Andean bellflower
decision_basis: Natural-history report supports mechanical mismatch interpretation but lacks the required quantitative geometry-to-route comparison/model.

title: Corolla Abscission Triggered by Nectar Robbers Positively Affects Reproduction by Enhancing Self-Pollination in Symphytum officinale (Boraginaceae)
decision_basis: Primary question is the consequence of nectar robbing for corolla abscission and reproduction, not an independently measured access-geometry predictor of robbery route use.
notes: Not a direct access-geometry -> robbery test.
